text:
julie: FYI AcmeOne wants a POC that supports session resumption for streaming (client can disconnect/reconnect and continue the same session). Also they insist on bounded batching so tail latency stays <150ms. Pricing and security are flagged as blockers. any guidance?

tariq: short answer: SDK + runtime already have reconnect hooks, but we don't have an opinionated session-resume protocol exposed in the public SDKs yet. we do support KV cache reuse and can reattach a token-context.

maria: for streaming resumption we typically rely on a session-id + last-token-index from the client. server keeps short-lived resume state (~60s) in memory or a small redis for dedicated deployments. works with prefix caching.

olivia: sales ask: does that affect hosted pricing? client worry is high token re-generation cost if we can't resume mid-stream.

kevin: hosted: resume reduces duplicated tokens so net cost often goes down, but we need to limit resume window to avoid indefinite state. pricing impact depends on how many resumed sessions exceed token thresholds. propose: treat resumed tokens as normal tokens (per-token billing) and offer a small monthly credit for trial POCs.

sam: security question from AcmeOne: do resumed sessions leak context cross-customers? they have SOC2 + legal concerns.

maria: resumption design note: session-id must be scoped to customer + model instance + ephemeral nonce. resume state never contains customer plaintext prompts; we store only KV cache deltas or token indices and a checksum. on hosted we encrypt resume blobs with KMS. on private/dedicated we recommend customer-managed KMS.

julie: can we give them a short runbook for the POC: steps, sample SDK code, and expected perf? they asked for a one-pager.

olivia: i can draft the runbook. need a small sample showing client reconnect header and server-side state TTL.

maria: sample reconnect header (client):

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
X-Redwood-Session: session_abc123
X-Redwood-Resume-Index: 3456
```

server side pseudo: keep resume-state keyed by session id + customer id, TTL 45s for hosted POC, fallback to prefix replay if expired.

kevin: infra note: for Dedicated we can increase TTL and persist resume state in a local redis cluster to support bursts. that avoids fetching from central store and keeps tail latency predictable.

julie: pricing ask again: what should i tell them for the POC estimate (1m tokens over 2 weeks, expect 6% resumes)?

kevin: rough: baseline token cost for 1m tokens + negligible extra for resume meta. if resumed tokens are within same 1m count no double billing. if resumes cause re-generation beyond 1m then bill additional tokens. propose: for POC cap, we can do flat trial credit covering up to 1.05x tokens to account for some replays.

olivia: legal: they also want answers in the security questionnaire about ephemeral storage and KMS usage. can we attach a short answer doc?

maria: short answers: hosted resume blobs encrypted with customer-scoped envelope keys, accessible only to the runtime service. audit logs show resume blob access. dedicated/private: customer-managed KMS + audit. mention that blobs are rotated and TTL enforced.

infra-bot: deploy note: there is a canary for resume-state feature in staging-poc cluster. tests: reconnect->resume success rate 98% under 100 concurrent streams.

sam: any caveats on structured output/tool-calls combined with resume? if a tool call triggered mid-stream and then client resumes, will tool state replay?

maria: tool-call side-effects are not replayed by default. we recommend idempotent tool design or include a tool-call checkpoint in resume metadata. for POC we can enable a "tool-call log" in dedicated so you can replay safely.

julie: perfect. olivia please draft the runbook + security Q answers and i'll attach the pricing note (kevin). i'll loop in legal if needed.

olivia: on it — will share a draft by EOD + example SDK snippet (node + go) for reconnect. :thumbsup:
